notes: Direct translation. rl2:grantor/grantee become the Agreement's assigner/assignee; by the compact-policy rule they apply to both rules, matching RL2's per-clause rl2:subject ex:Licensee. RL2 states no conflict strategy in the policy; odrl:prohibit is made explicit (it does not matter here, since the two rules never match the same action). Scenarios 3 and 4 are added. Scenario 4 shows that a request naming no assignee leaves the prohibition U, so due2 does not deny it outright. No divergence from RL2.

expected.why: ex:noTraining applies (action, target, assignee all T). ex:searchCorpus fails on action, so there is no candidate; the T Forbid gives Deny.
ex:searchCorpus is T with no duties, so it is a ready candidate; ex:noTraining fails on action.

scenarios.name: a third party trains a model

expected.why: ex:Stranger ⊑ ex:Licensee is F, so the prohibition does not apply; the agreement binds only its assignee. No permission applies either.
The request names no assignee, so the prohibition's party part is U (§5.2) and ex:noTraining is U. No candidate exists. The restrictive completion gives Deny, the permissive one NotApplicable.
